summary.short: Danish supplementary act to the EU AI Act (Regulation (EU) 2024/1689). Designates Digitaliseringsstyrelsen, Datatilsynet and Domstolsstyrelsen as national competent and market surveillance authorities, gives them inspection and order powers, and sets fines and criminal liability for listed breaches. In force 2 August 2025.
summary.long: Supplements the EU AI Act (Regulation (EU) 2024/1689), reproduced as Annex 1. Designates Digitaliseringsstyrelsen, Datatilsynet and Domstolsstyrelsen as national competent and market surveillance authorities, with Digitaliseringsstyrelsen also acting as authorising authority and single point of contact. Market surveillance authorities may demand information, enter business premises without a court order, carry out technical inspections, publish decisions on prohibited AI practices, issue compliance orders, and impose temporary bans on supplying an AI system that poses a risk. The minister may, after negotiation, set rules for notified conformity assessment bodies. Breaches of the Article 5 prohibitions, false or misleading information, non-compliance with information demands, orders or temporary bans, and obstruction of access are punishable by fines; legal persons may be criminally liable under the Criminal Code; the limitation period is five years. Fine orders may be issued without trial where the offender admits guilt and agrees to pay. The act enters into force on 2 August 2025 and does not apply to the Faroe Islands or Greenland.

notes: Part 1 of 4: covers §§ 1-13 of the Danish Act and the start of Bilag 1. Bilag 1 reproduces the EU AI Regulation (2024/1689) for convenience; its recitals are not annotated as Danish law. Footnote 1 states that the reproduction does not affect the Regulation's direct applicability. The ministerial rule-making powers in §§ 9 and 11 are delegations; the rules themselves are not part of this text. Target instrument IDs are empty because the EU Regulation and the other statutes are not in the registry; the names are in target_text. The section_status entries below are included only to satisfy the schema; entries are recorded above. This part contains no separately numbered provisions of the Danish act as far as the text shows. It reproduces recitals (141)-(180) and Articles 1-52(4) of the EU artificial intelligence regulation as printed; the coded relations and entities come from that reproduced text. Target instrument IDs are left empty because the document gives no registry IDs for the EU acts it cites. Recital (158) and Art. 17(4) refer to EU financial-services law in general and name specific directives only in recital (158); these are not coded. National competent, market surveillance and notifying authorities are designated by Member States under Art. 28 and Art. 3(19), (26) and (48) but are not named in this part. Part 3 of 4 (Arts. 53-113, Annexes I-IX and footnotes) reproduces the Danish text of Regulation (EU) 2024/1689. It contains no separate Danish national provisions. Relations and entities record only what this text states; target_instrument_id is left empty because registry IDs were not supplied. Art. 102-110 amend other EU instruments as stated in the reproduced text. Part 4 of 4 contains only annexes: an unnumbered annex on registration of testing under real conditions (heading shown without a number in this part), Annex X (EU large-scale IT system acts, coded as 12 relation rows), and Annexes XI to XIII (general-purpose AI model documentation, transparency information and systemic-risk designation criteria). The document gives no numbering for the first annex in this part. Annex XIII point (f) states that a model is presumed to have a large impact on the internal market when made available to at least 10 000 registered business users established in the Union (presumption wording 'formodes'); it is not coded as a threshold here, since thresholds are outside the scope requested for this part. Annex XI and XII contain no dates or thresholds.
